To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the systematics power spectra are strongly redshift-dependent, with the most important contributions coming from the multiplicative bias, while the additive bias is sub-dominant; the amplitude of the multiplicative bias scales approximately as the source ellipticity; the systematics power is dominated by the angular scale range between 1 and 10 arcminutes; and the bias on the cosmological parameters is significant, especially for modified gravity theories.
systematics in cosmic-shear tomography can be described in terms of multiplicative and additive biases, which are both redshift dependent.

the power spectrum of shear measurement systematics can be efficiently computed by means of analytical expressions, and that even a modest amount of systematics can bias the inferred cosmological constraints.

, if we do not want to be fooled, we should be careful in our measurements and in our analysis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the power spectrum of systematic errors can be estimated with our method, which can then be used in the analysis of the cosmic shear data to estimate the systematic bias on cosmological measurements.
, in order to avoid biases, it is necessary to control systematics to a precision of the order of 1%, which is a challenging task.
the impact of shear systematics on the inferred cosmology is non-negligble and has to be properly taken into account.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when performing a tomographic weak lensing analysis, it is important to account not only for the systematics uncertainties in each tomographic bin, but also for their covariance across different redshift bins.

, in order to obtain unbiased constraints on cosmological parameters, systematics have to be carefully accounted for in the analysis, especially in the case of future surveys with a very high number of source galaxies.
systematics in the power spectrum of shear can be efficiently computed and propagated to the inferred parameters.
